questions.text: I focus on creating the conditions for a great present and let the future emerge from that.
I notice when two people have developed private shorthand or inside references that exclude others in the group.
I routinely pick up litter, fix broken things, and tidy shared spaces without being asked.
I set recurring calendar events for tasks that need to happen regularly.
I feel most capable when authority is shared across team members in a domain.
Knowing that someone will keep suffering rarely bothers me.
I instinctively adapt to whatever structure the group has established.
I establish naming conventions for my files so I can search for them easily.
Once I know that someone is in serious pain, their wellbeing matters a great deal to me.
I routinely make lifestyle choices that reflect my personal standards and aspirations.
I notice that my hands stay steady and my voice stays even in situations that rattle other people.
I am often less concerned about other people's troubles than the people around me are.
I often cancel my own plans to help a friend, colleague, or family member.
I tend to miss the warning signs that a conversation is heading toward conflict.
I am comfortable unilaterally canceling plans that I think are not working.
I rarely sense when a social environment has an implicit dress code or behavioral code that I am violating.
I notice when a group's laughter is directed at someone rather than shared with them.
I notice that when multiple emotions arrive at once, the overload can feel physically paralyzing.
After an emotionally charged event, I feel like I need to recover as if from physical exertion.
I can tell when a couple is mid-argument even though they are being perfectly civil in public.
I proactively recruit people to my initiatives.
Another person's wellbeing matters to me even when I do not feel close to them.
I let each morning develop its own rhythm instead of front-loading priority tasks.
I rarely sense when someone is tailoring their message based on who is listening.
I can remain focused and clearheaded even in high-pressure situations.
I experience the surprise of being startled not as a brief jolt but as a lingering rush of adrenaline.
I tend to let the group decide when the meeting wraps and what the next steps are.
I routinely accept the worst option for myself so that others can have the better one.
I feel a genuine sense of accomplishment when I execute a plan exactly as designed.
I routinely treat myself to experiences and products that bring me personal joy.
I tend to choose mentors and advisors based on how they can accelerate my personal growth.
I throw things together at the last minute and it usually works out fine.
It is hard for me to turn away from someone's pain, even when I can't fix it.
A person's suffering rarely changes what I hope will happen for them.
I experience daily frustrations — traffic, delays, minor inconveniences — without a noticeable rise in my stress level.
I enjoy the weight of responsibility that comes with leading.
